summary: Anuj Misra studied under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker from around 2012 to 2016.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Calcutta, studying under Nalinaksha Dutt and Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya. He held posts at the University of Calcutta and directed the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.
Anuradha Seneviratna worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peradeniya from around 1958 to 1963 and later served there as a professor from circa 1965 to 2004.

Archibald Edward Gough worked in Indology and philosophy after studying under Monier Monier-Williams. His posts included Anglo-Sanskrit Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1868–1878), Professor of Philosophy at Presidency University (1878–1881), and Principal of Aliah University (1881–1886).
Ariane Macdonald worked in Tibetology and Sinology. She studied under Rolf Alfred Stein and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1972).

Arindam Chakrabarti is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford. He served as a professor of philosophy at the University of Delhi (attested 1999) and at the University of Hawaiʻi (attested 2009–2014).
Arinde L. Jonker works in Indology and religious studies. She completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), studying under Peter C. Bisschop, Daniele Cuneo, and Jonathan A. Silk.
Aristotle C. Dy, a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, completed his PhD at SOAS University of London (attested 2013) under the doctoral supervision of Antonello Palumbo.

Arjo Vanderjagt studied philosophy at the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He later held academic posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), the University of Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

Arlo Griffiths specializes in Indology, linguistics, and archaeology. He studied at Harvard and Leiden University under Michael Witzel, Henk Bodewitz, and Alexander Lubotsky, later holding professorships at Leiden University (attested 2002–2008) and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (from 2008).

Arnold J. Toynbee was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Winchester College and Balliol College, Oxford. He held posts at King's College London (1919–1924), Chatham House (1925–1955), and the London School of Economics (1925–1955).

Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Tübingen, Leipzig, and Oxford under Theodor Benfey, Rudolf von Roth, and Friedrich Max Müller. He was Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1888 to 1899.

Arthur Berriedale Keith, an Indologist and linguist, studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, under Julius Eggeling and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served in the Colonial Office (1901–1914) and as Professor at Edinburgh (1914–1944).

Arthur Christensen was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding the chair of Oriental studies at Copenhagen from 1919 to 1945.

Arthur Coke Burnell worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at King's College London and under Theodor Goldstücker, Heinrich August Jäschke, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, serving in the Indian Civil Service from 1860 to 1880.
Arthur Evans was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Harrow School (circa 1865–1870) and Brasenose College (1870).

Arthur F. Wright specialized in Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies, studying at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard under John King Fairbank. He held professorships at Stanford University (1947–1958) and Yale University (1959, 1961).

Arthur Llewellyn Basham was a historian and Indologist who studied under Lionel David Barnett at SOAS. He held posts as Professor at SOAS and later head of Asian Civilizations at the Australian National University (~1965–1978).

Arthur McKeown is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and scholar of Buddhist studies. He was a doctoral candidate at Harvard University (attested 2005), where he studied under Parimal G. Patil, Palri Sangye, and Diana L. Eck.

Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Jena under Friedrich Majer, Friedrich Schleiermacher, August Boeckh, and Friedrich August Wolf. He held a lecturing post at the University of Berlin in 1820.
